sections.title: AI & ML
sections.body: Amazon Acquires DuckLabs and Integrates DuckDB in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (InfoQ). Replit is no longer working with Anthropic, CEO says (TechCrunch AI). A 24-second template beats infinite control (for a first version) (Dev.to AI). Jev Router Benchmark: 117 of 118 Calls Went to GPT-6.1 Sol (Dev.to AI). How Long Before Your Agent Says Anything? digest.key_takeaway: Amazon has acquired DuckLabs, the company behind the analytical database DuckDB. Co-founders Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt will continue to lead the team under AWS. The acquisition aims to enhance the development and reach of DuckDB while maintaining its open-source status. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL gets its first DuckDB-powered feature following the acquisition. By Gianmarco Nalin

articles.summary: Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer with Anthropic.

articles.title: A 24-second template beats infinite control (for a first version)
articles.summary:
Every AI video tool starts with a control panel. Mine started with a fixed template, and that was the only reason it shipped.


  
  
  Infinite control is a trap for a first release


When the first version exposes duration, motion, style, aspect ratio and seed, you are not giving the user power — you are giving them decisions they cannot evaluate. Users cannot tell a good seed from a bad one. They can tell whether the result looks right.

A fixed template makes the first release testable: one input, one output shape, one thing to judge.

articles.summary:
TypeSafe's Jev Router (typesafe/jev-router on OpenRouter) went to the top of our Forge 2.0 agentic coding benchmark this morning. articles.title: My PDF-to-Markdown converter kept flattening two-column papers into soup — column detection was the whole game
articles.summary:
I built the PDF-to-Markdown API expecting layout to be a solved problem. It isn't.

The failure mode was subtle and brutal: academic papers with two-column layouts came back as interleaved garbage. Line one of column A, line one of column B, line two of column A... The Markdown looked fine at a glance — headings, paragraphs, lists all present — but the reading order was destroyed. I fed one into a RAG pipeline and the retriever started quoting sentences that spanned two unrelated columns. The chunks were technically valid; semantically they were nonsense.

articles.title: Helidon 27 Introduces Restructured Programming Models and New Messaging and Data Modules
articles.summary: The release of Helidon 27 is the first release that follows the Oracle Tip & Tail Model of Library Development by which the Tip adopts the latest Java technology while the Tail provides a more stable and secure baseline. Concurrent with the release of JDK 27, new features in Helidon 27 include: an introduction to new major modules, Helidon Messaging and Helidon Data JDBC. By Michael Redlich

articles.title: Valid JSON Is Not Conformant JSON: Five Free-Model Myths and a Pass-Rate Probe
articles.summary:
A worker dies at 2 a.m. The payload parses fine. Nobody believes the alert at first.

That gap — parses versus conforms — is where a lot of free-model pipelines quietly break. I keep seeing the same five claims in review threads. Each one is testable in under an hour.

Here is the probe I reach for, and the mental model I would swap in.


  
  
  Myth 1: "If json.loads accepts it, the model followed my schema."


No. You have two gates. Most teams install only the first one.



Gate A — parse. Is the text a JSON value at all?

articles.title: [Research] 2,788 tokens/s on a single RTX 5090 with a diffusion LLM — Introducing ORL (fully open source) [R]
articles.summary: Hey r/MachineLearning! We're excited to share ORL (On-Policy Residual Learning), our new research on making diffusion language models (dLLMs) significantly faster without sacrificing generation quality. With ORL and our custom inference engine dlmrt, we've achieved:  2,788 tokens/s on a single RTX 5090 — LLaDA-2.1-mini + ORL, NVFP4 7,708 tokens/s on 8× B200 — DiffusionGemma 26B MoE + ORL, NVFP4 Up to 6.9× higher end-to-end throughput on our QwenDLM-4B model, at comparable or better quality 1.74× faster than DFlash speculative decoding at matched accuracy in our single-request H100 comparison

articles.title: Go Profiling in Production: pprof, Flamegraphs and Memory Leaks
Chainguard Launches Secure Workspaces and Checks for AI Coding Agents
articles.summary: Software supply chain security company Chainguard has announced two beta products for running and testing code written by developers and AI agents. Chainguard Workspaces provides remote development environments based on hardened microVMs, while Chainguard Checks moves continuous integration into the development loop. The company announced both products at its Assemble London event. By Matt Saunders

articles.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
articles.summary: According to Elorian's evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.

articles.title: Zod Brings In-Process Schema Compilation and a 9x Cut in Memory Footprint
articles.summary: Zod is a TypeScript-focused schema validation library that recently released versions 4.5 and 4.6. Key updates include schema compilation for faster data parsing, significant memory usage reductions, and new validation features. The library supports efficient validation processes and remains popular in the JavaScript ecosystem, achieving millions of downloads weekly. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: AWS Introduces Strands Decider 2B and Strands Box for AI Agent Development
articles.summary: AWS has introduced two open-source projects for AI agent development: Strands Decider 2B, a small model designed to make decisions within agent workflows, and Strands Box, a sandbox for controlling agent execution. Both projects address different aspects of building agents that use tools, execute code, and interact with external systems. By Daniel Dominguez

articles.title: Google EnvHarness Enables Self-Evolving Agents to Learn in Dynamics Environments
articles.summary: Google researchers open sourced EnvHarness, a framework that dynamically adapts agent-training environments to an agent's weaknesses without modifying the agent, environment, or evaluation system. According to the researchers, this approach can improve both learning effectiveness and efficiency while helping agents overcome their weaknesses. By Sergio De Simone

articles.title: Microsoft Commits Maia to Multi-Gigawatt Inference, and Its Efficiency Metric Draws Questions
articles.summary: Microsoft will scale its Maia accelerator family to multi-gigawatt deployments from 2027, making it the primary inference system for its own products. Maia 300 collapses scale-up and scale-out onto one Ethernet fabric and moves KV state between prefill and decode workers without leaving it. Practitioners have questioned the tokens-per-watt claim that leads the announcement. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
